latest_release.name: TensorFold 1.2.9
latest_release.body:
# TensorFold 1.2.9

1.2.9 brings faster decode and long prompts, an Ollama-compatible API, and fixes for a wrong reply and a hang. Every
speedup below keeps replies unchanged.

## Speed

- **Nemotron on Metal** (without an MTP head): concurrent streams share one round. On an M5 Ultra, two streams decode
  about 20% faster, four about 75%, eight 2.3 to 2.5 times and 24 streams 3.2 to 3.5 times (#3005).
- **GLM-5.3-Flash on CUDA:**
  - Long prompts' first token comes 0.6% to 13.7% sooner at TP=3 from 131,072 to 2,000,000 tokens, and 6.7% sooner at
    TP=2 at 1,000,000; shorter prompts at TP=2 stay within about 2% either way (#3159).
  - After a 1,040,384-token prompt, decode rounds are 5.05%, 9.36% and 11.36% shorter at 1, 4 and 8 streams (#2722).
- **Qwen3.8-Flash-Next on HIP** (gfx1151): one stream decodes about 6% faster, four streams 2.8% to 4.6% (#2697).
- **Fewer CUDA launches** for Flash Next draws (#2927), Nemotron 3.5 draws (15 a level instead of about 112, #3124) and
  Qwen3.8-27B prompts (#2925).

## Models and features

- **An Ollama-compatible API:** `/api/chat`, `/api/generate`, `/api/embed`, `/api/tags`, `/api/show`, `/api/ps` and
  `/api/version` on the same engine paths as the OpenAI routes (#3342).
- **`tensorfold serve --config FILE.toml`** reads serve flags from a file, so a launch can be checked in (#2885).
- **Linux:** an opt-in memory-pressure governor driven by PSI, `TENSORFOLD_MEMORY_PRESSURE=1` (#2156).
- **Groundwork, not used by any served model yet:** a CUDA image path for the dense engine (#2768), dots.mocr's vision
  kernels (#2767), and HIP's TCP fabric for two hosts without RDMA (#2961).
- **An experimental Living Weights v2 controller** in `tools/living_weights_v2` (#3320).

## Server and API

- `/v1/models` lists each model's `input_types`. A video sent to a model without video is a 400, not a 500 (#3019).
- Logprobs work with tools, stop strings and reasoning, and on the Responses API (#3206).
- With thinking off, a request's reasoning effort reaches the template (#3017).
- Replies say when they kept a tool call as text, in `tensorfold.kept_tool_calls` and two `/metrics` counters (#2814).
- Streams can carry the committed token IDs, opt-in (#3285).

## Fixes

- **Nemotron Omni on CUDA:** a failed image request no longer leaks into the next reply (#2985).
- **GLM-5.3-Flash at TP=3:** `prompt_logprobs` over about 100 tokens no longer hangs (#1571).
- **Living Weights:** the drift gate no longer refuses a lesson over the writer's own wording (#2929).
- **CUDA:** the release server refuses a GPU it has no kernels for, by name, at startup (#2914).

## For developers

- `zig build test-host` gathers the Linux host checks (#2095); flaky tests fixed (#2963, #3015, #3310, #3347, #3349,
  #3355); docs for `TF_GLM_PROF` (#2990) and a Jammed XSFP4 NZ5 row (#2981).

## What changes by default

- **GLM on CUDA:** the `TF_GLM_INDEX_CUDA` kernels and `TF_GLM_DSEL` are on by default.
- **Flash Next on CUDA:** sampled draws are batched by default; `TF_FLASHNEXT_BATCH_DRAWS=0` restores per-stream draws.
- **Flash Next on HIP:** on one RDNA 3.5 GPU (gfx1150 to gfx1153) serving alone, MTP drafts stop under a 0.8
  confidence floor; other HIP GPUs and families keep 0.3, and `--mtp-confidence` still overrides it.
- **Server:** `--reasoning-effort` no longer changes a thinking-off prompt.
- **Server:** a `video_url` part sent to a model without video gets HTTP 400 (`invalid_request_error`), not a 500.
- **CUDA:** the release server refuses, by name at startup, a GPU it has no kernels for.

The first three keep replies unchanged. The fourth changes the prompt of a thinking-off request when the server sets
`--reasoning-effort`. The last two turn a failure into a named refusal.

## Thanks

@Bizuayeu, @Defilan, @garvrao80, @gilby, @jimthedj65, @jishnuvenugopal, @laudney, Mia's AI Lab (@MiaAI-Lab),
@Nipale-ai, @Shoestring-dev, @ss-cong, @tarsnake and @WebReflection.

Help Support TensorFold · @tensorfold_dev on X

# TensorFold TensorFold serves language models from a Zig binary on Apple Silicon and NVIDIA GPUs. The engine reads checkpoints, tokenizes requests and runs Metal or CUDA kernels directly. Serving needs no Python or MLX installation. Building with a coding agent? Have it load the [contributor skill](docs/recipes/SKILL.md) and follow [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md#contributing-with-agents). ## Quick start Start with Qwen3.5-2B, a small 4-bit checkpoint. The commands below download its pinned revision, then serve it as `local-model`. Model weights have their own licenses. ### Mac with Apple Silicon Install with Homebrew, then start the server: ```sh brew install ashhart/tensorfold/tensorfold tensorfold pull mlx-community/Qwen3.5-2B-MLX-4bit@93760be4f1f69842a46bc13dbdc0f19e291392a3 tensorfold serve mlx-community/Qwen3.5-2B-MLX-4bit --name local-model --context 8192 --no-thinking ``` ### Linux with an NVIDIA GPU Needs glibc 2.28 or newer and NVIDIA driver R580 or newer (CUDA 13.0). The [run guide](docs/run-guide.md#platform-setup) lists the archive's requirements; Windows has [its own guide](docs/WINDOWS.md). ```sh V=1.2.9 case "$(uname -m)" in aarch64|arm64) PLATFORM=linux-aarch64 ;; x86_64) PLATFORM=linux-x86_64 ;; *) echo 'No release archive for this CPU' >&2; exit 1 ;; esac curl -fLO "https://github.com/ashhart/TensorFold/releases/download/v$V/tensorfold-$V-$PLATFORM.tar.gz" curl -fLO "https://github.com/ashhart/TensorFold/releases/download/v$V/tensorfold-$V-$PLATFORM.tar.gz.sha256" sha256sum -c "tensorfold-$V-$PLATFORM.tar.gz.sha256" tar -xzf "tensorfold-$V-$PLATFORM.tar.gz" export PATH="$PWD/tensorfold-$V-$PLATFORM/bin:$PATH" tensorfold() { command tensorfold-native "$@"; } tensorfold pull mlx-community/Qwen3.5-2B-MLX-4bit@93760be4f1f69842a46bc13dbdc0f19e291392a3 tensorfold serve mlx-community/Qwen3.5-2B-MLX-4bit --name local-model --context 8192 --no-thinking ``` ### Send a request Leave the server running. In another terminal, on either platform: ```sh curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/chat/completions \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"model":"local-model","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Say hello in one sentence."}],"max_tokens":128,"temperature":0}' ``` The API also serves completions, Responses and Anthropic Messages. `/v1/models` lists the served name. ## Docs - [Run guide](docs/run-guide.md): platform setup, requests, parallel requests, exact decoding, context compaction, Cortheon mode, every serve flag, the Mac app and TensorFold Starlight. - [Supported models](docs/supported-models.md): which checkpoints run on which machines, models on disk and model discovery. - [Living Weights (experimental)](docs/living-weights.md): teach a running model new facts in its own weights. - [Installation runbook](RUNBOOK.md): macOS and CUDA installation, paired Metal serving and troubleshooting. - [Windows](docs/WINDOWS.md), [TensorFold Web](docs/web.md) and [the Mac app](app/README.md). - [API](docs/api.md), [Cortheon mode](docs/cortheon.md) and [known issues](docs/known-issues.md). - [Evaluating TensorFold](docs/evaluating.md) and [community benchmarks](docs/community-benchmarks.md). - [Usable memory profiles](docs/memory-profiling.md): how to record applied budgets, context, cache state and process peaks. - [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md): ATC and agents, builds, tests and the exactness and performance gates. - [Changes](CHANGELOG.md), [1.0.0 release notes](docs/release-notes-1.0.0.md) and [the Zig engine preview](docs/zig-preview.md). - TensorFold is Apache-2.0: [LICENSE](LICENSE), [NOTICE](NOTICE), [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md) and [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md). ## Contributors Thank you to everyone who has sent TensorFold a pull request, a measurement or a bug report:
